description.purpose: The agent core as one template (GH #28, R-CG-1/R-CG-2): a hive that references collector@5.1.0 as `collector`, curator@1.6.0 as `curator` and dispatcher@1.2.2 as `dispatcher` plus ONE llm brain slot and the cell that declares the core's own errand, with every internal edge pre-wired - the seam with its own iteration bound and its own restore_ttl, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback. Structurally a talky without a channel: no session-keeper, no summarizer, no proxy, because the core has no channel, no sessions and no night. Its conversation is the errands the channel voices send it. Since 4.1.0 the curator is LIVE here and nowhere else (GH #451): the collector ships with `context_window` set instead of 0, because a cogny is the shape the curator was built for - few turns, huge tool results - while a channel voice is the other one. The `thread_recall` lane it needs comes with it: `./dispatcher -> ./collector` on the reserved tool name, which is the second reserved name the guarded default exit of 4.0.2 was designed to cost exactly one ordinary edge. Without that lane a stub is a dead end, so the two land together or not at all. Since 4.2.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) the composite carries the lane its own seal made impossible: `in_pack`, from the hive path through the collector into the brain, where a pack of durable `system.*` slots becomes an upsert into its own `cell.db`. It needed `collector@3.2.0` and answers every pack ONCE on `pack_ack`, paired in `required_drains`. Since `4.3.0` ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)) the core asks the tools hive what its tools look like instead of carrying a typed menu: it declares `["*"]` -- a reasoning core should reach everything its surface can, and a list typed here would be a second copy of a catalogue that drifts on the first tool added -- the request leaves on `schemas` and the answer comes back on `in_menu`, written into `./brain` as durable `system.tools`. Since `4.4.0` ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)) the core is the PROBLEM SOLVER and only that, and it costs one cell slot, one lane pair and one knob. ONE brain: `brain_fast`, `escalate_to_deep` and the `consult_class` lookup lane are gone, because the right owner of a fast memory question is the conversation surface that already holds the window -- routing it through an advisor was the round trip GH #124 measured. WHOEVER IS REACHED DECLARES THEMSELVES: `in_schemas` in, `tool_schemas` out, the tools hive's own lane pair and answer shape, carrying exactly one schema -- `consult_cogny` with `question` and `context` both REQUIRED, `eta` and `consult_id` optional -- whose description is the class boundary. Without it the `consult_cogny` declaration had no owner at all after #464 and a grown caller offered its model a menu without the one tool the core exists for. And the memory leg is a TOOL: since 5.0.0 (GH #552) `memory_recall` is an ORDINARY tool name that leaves this composite for the member's own memory, which declares and answers it, while `memory_tier` stays empty -- a problem solver asks about a time range or a session on purpose and is not handed an ambient bundle it did not ask for. A removed cell slot is a contract change and a new accepted lane is additive; both are the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Also in `4.4.0` ([#539](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/539)) the "without a channel" above is enforced instead of merely stated: the dispatcher ships with `interim` off. A thinking model puts a sentence next to its tool bundle -- "I am checking the official fares now" -- and the dispatcher used to send it on the answer lane, which for THIS composite is the advice lane of the voice that asked. So the voice was handed an advisor's answer that was not one, said it to the user, and sometimes consulted again; the core answered with its next interim sentence. Measured on a live colony: 11 of 26 answers on that lane were interim, and one user turn produced thirteen messages. Off, the sentence does not leave the dispatcher at all and does not enter the core's own window either -- a sentence nobody could hear was never said -- while the FINAL answer is untouched. One knob on a ref, no lane and no cell -- and the version does not move, because 4.4.0 is unreleased and an unreleased entry is amended in place. Since `4.5.0` ([#548](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/548)) the cell answering `in_schemas` is `./schemas`, not `./declare`. ONE LANE, ONE CELL NAME: `templates/tools` answers the same lane pair with a cell called `schemas`, this core answered it with a cell called `declare`, and the two scripts differ in their schema table and almost nowhere else -- `declare`'s own header comment said the lane pair and the answer shape were the tools hive's, byte for byte. Every `override_params` path, every mutation adding a schema and every reader following the declaration round then had to know which of the two words this particular hive picked, and a third hive would have picked a third. `schemas` is the survivor because it names what comes back and it matches the lane. A renamed cell slot is the hive's own address space, so it is the second digit by the same reading that made 4.4.0 one (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4). Since 4.6.0 the rim declares the two halves of the CREDENTIAL LANE and names `./brain` as their connect point (GH #560): `emits.credential_request` and `accepts.in_sealed`, both carrying `at: ["./brain"]`. That lets the member level draw the lane as a v-lane (GH #559) straight from the brain to the person's own `access`, instead of a pass-through chain through three rims -- and it lets a brain run on `params.credential_grant_id` with no key in its config at all. A caller can now dock something it could never dock before, so it is the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 4.6.1 the collector ref carries the partial answer (GH #570): a research-sized errand that reaches `max_iter` now leaves on `answer` with a named partial answer as its last turn and `hop.partial == "1"` beside `hop.round_capped`, instead of with the raw end of the tool round -- which the asking voice used to receive as the advice itself. Only the pin moves -- no lane, no port, no param of this template. Since 5.0.0 the menu is re-asked on the MUTATION RECEIPT rather than on a five-minute tick (GH #553): the composite declares `mutation_committed` at its own rim -- the lane keeps ONE name from the mutation door down to the collector -- and carries it inwards with one edge of its own. The collector's `menu-clock` is gone. Since 5.0.0 every behaviour knob of this composite is a PARAM of the cell that reads it -- the collector's since `collector@1.2.0`, the dispatcher's since `dispatcher@1.2.0`, and the brain's `credential_grant_id` as a literal empty string here ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138), ruling R-0904-6). What stays in `.env` is the provider lane: the API key, the endpoint and the model id. 5.0.1 re-points the collector ref at `collector@4.1.0`, whose block contract is composed from the sections its answerers OFFER instead of a literal it carries ([#606](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/606)). Only the pin moves: this core has no splitter, so it offers nothing, asks for nothing and behaves exactly as 5.0.0 did. 5.0.2 moves that pin twice more, to `collector@4.2.0`, and nothing else: the collector has since grown the `in_delegation` lane and the `advise` assembly mode a duplex call needs (welle-live, [#784](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/784)), neither of which this core's rim declares, so nothing it does changes. 5.0.3 moves it to `collector@4.2.1` ([#728](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/728)) and gives the brain the OpenRouter app attribution (`http_referer` / `x_title`, in the form of the memory-hive cells, overridable by `OPENROUTER_HTTP_REFERER` / `OPENROUTER_X_TITLE`) -- before, every request of a core reached the provider without naming its app. A reference resolves EXACTLY, so a pin left behind is a template that stops instantiating -- which is why a pin follow-up is a repair and the third digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). 5.0.4 moves the pin to `collector@4.3.0` ([#834](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/834)) and nothing else: the brief leg is off in this core (`brief_slots` stays empty), because only a surface opens a turn with a counterpart. 5.1.0 moves the pins to `collector@4.4.0` and `dispatcher@1.2.1` ([#843](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/843), [#842](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/842)): the core's `length` edge still goes straight to its collector -- a core has no splitter -- and the answer it produces now carries `hop.finish_reason` and `hop.truncated = "1"`, so whoever asked can tell a cut advice from a finished one. It is the second digit. 5.1.3 moves the pins to `collector@4.4.1` and `dispatcher@1.2.2` ([#871](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/871)) and nothing else: that collector shows every earlier answer with the block a splitter cut out of it, and a core has no splitter, so no answer brings a block along and its window stays what it was. Only the pins move, which is the third digit. 5.1.4 declares `hop.model` on `brain` ([#886](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/886)) and nothing else: the cell always wrote the model the provider served into the header, and the contract now says so, in the one wording the library uses. The third digit. 5.2.0 references `curator` and moves the window, the curation and the identity pack from the collector to it ([#889](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/889)); no lane of the boundary moved, the `in_model` door now also reaches the curator's summarizer, and `brain` declares every hop key the `llm` cell writes into an answer, the cache keys among them ([#890](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/890)), so it is the second digit. 5.3.0 cuts its own block and can ask back ([#892](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/892), [#893](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/893), [#894](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/894), [#895](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/895)): a splitter like talky's hands every section to the curator, which runs as role `consult`; the `history_*` tools are answered inside; the new cell `./ask` turns an `ask_requester` call into the question that leaves on the new route `ask`, and the collector runs with `defer_turns` `"0"`, so an errand or a reply that arrives during an open tool round opens a round of its own. It moves the `curator` pin to 1.1.0 and the `collector` pin to 5.1.0. A route joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. 5.3.1 moves the `curator` pin to 1.1.1 ([#904](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/904)): the curator's cache clock keeps one standing order instead of adding one per call. Only the pin moved, so it is the third digit. 5.5.0 ([#925](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/925), [#926](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/926)) carries `in_stats` to its curator and `stats` back out, and moves the `curator` pin to 1.3.0, whose ledger knows the audience of every row. A lane joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 5.6.0 ([#932](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/932), [#935](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/935)) `in_pack` takes five families, `identity_short` among them, and the `curator` pin moves to 1.4.0, whose readers select only rows the round may see. A caller can do what it could not before, so it is the second digit. Since 5.6.1 ([#941](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/941)) the brain edge passes the `episode_turn_id` that talky set on the consult through unchanged (cogny writes no episode of its own) and the `curator` pin moves to 1.4.1; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 5.6.2 ([#943](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/943)) the `curator` pin moves to 1.5.0; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 5.7.0 ([#949](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/949)) the curator's lanes `in_candidate` and `in_read` enter the core and `candidate_ack`, `read` and `thing_seen` leave it, and the `curator` pin moves to 1.6.0. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 5.7.1 the pin moves to `curator@1.7.0`; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 5.8.0 ([#980](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/980)) both curator-entry edges bind `hop.iter < 20`, the collector runs with `max_iter` 16 and `round_idle_ms` 630000, `./brain` declares `hop.dropped` ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) and the pin moves to `curator@1.7.1`. A longer bound is a promise the core never made, so it is the second digit. Since 5.8.1 ([#999](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/999)) `./brain` declares the optional hop key `unverified`, the sampling fields sent without a `supported_params` list to check them and the pin moves to `curator@1.8.0`; no lane moved, so it is the third digit.
description.use_when: One per agent, never one per channel voice - a sibling hive of the channel voices at agent level (<agent>/{talky..., cogny, memory, archive}). Instantiate via add_nodes AND wire the consult port pair, the declaration port pair and the tool, memory and error lanes via add_edges IN THE SAME MUTATION; the composite is an island until an edge crosses into it. The ingress edge MUST promote `session_id` into context - the `in_turn` lane declares it, because the core's memory tool asks about sessions. Instantiation needs ctx.model (the THINKING model - a fast channel model there wastes the split); it takes a resolved literal or a MODEL_<ROLE> env token passed verbatim. `ctx.model_fast` is gone since 4.4.0 and an instantiation that still passes it is not refused, it is simply ignored.
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells - the tool set is the per-agent choice and its lanes are wired per instance on hop.tool_name. No session keeper, no proxy, no channel identity, no persona: cogny mints no id, closes no day and speaks to no user. No memory hive either - the recall/in_bundle pair is wired to the central hive from the parent scope, the core only asks. And no errors cell: the brain's failures are put on the error lane by the exit edge, not by a unit of this composite. And no classifier and no second lane since 4.4.0: there is ONE class of errand, so nothing anywhere picks between two. And `in_pack` is not an open write channel into the prompt: four slot names (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions` since [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488)), checked against a constant in the curator, owner off the envelope. Who may OPEN such a lane is decided further out -- the edge is a mutation, and `templates/submit` checks its form while the broker answers the capability `affinity.subscribe` (GH #458). And no tool SCHEMAS of other people's tools: since 4.3.0 this core ASKS for those, which is not the same as owning them -- they live in the tools hive beside the cells they describe (GH #464). The one schema it does own is its OWN errand ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)), which is the same rule read from the other side. And no interim answers since 4.4.0 (#539): this core emits ONE answer per consultation -- the result on the answer lane, or, since GH #894, a question back on its own `ask` lane under the same `consult_id` -- and never a sentence about the work in progress.
examples: PORTS - Consult ingress, ONE lane since 4.4.0, landing on the hive path with route in_turn: the asking dispatcher's edge on hop.tool_name == 'consult_cogny' and, since #894, a second one on 'reply_to_consult' (the asker's answer to a question this core asked back). Each MUST promote hop.consult_id to context, MUST carry `session_id` in context (the lane declares it), and MUST clear col_phase, otherwise the correlation dies at the next hop and the errand arrives mid-assembly. Advice exit: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' -> the asking voice's collector on lane in_advice, again clearing col_phase. Question exit (#894): the hive path on hop.route=='ask' -> the same lane in_advice of the voice that asked, promoting hop.consult_id and clearing col_phase. Five further lanes meet at the same path and are wired per instance: tool out / in_tool back for each tool cell (hop.tool_name says which one; `memory_recall` was reserved until 5.0.0 and LEAVES now, to the member's own memory hive, which declares the schema and answers the call ([#552](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/552))), recall out / in_bundle back for the central memory hive - the AMBIENT leg, and the only meaning that pair has since 5.0.0; `memory_tier` is empty here, so the shipped core fires it never - and error out, which the parent MUST drain: a failed inference is normalised onto it by the exit edge itself, because this composite carries no errors cell.

DECLARATION PORT - the second pair, and it is one decision: `./talky -> ./cogny` stamping `in_schemas` with the body `{"tools": ["consult_cogny"]}` (or `["*"]`), and `./cogny -> ./talky` on hop.route=='tool_schemas' into the asker's `in_menu`. The asker's collector cuts this answer together with the tools hive's; both answer in the same provider-neutral `{name, description, parameters}` shape, so neither of them has to know which provider the caller talks to

a consult errand arrives with question AND context -> the core runs its OWN tool round, asking its memory by TOOL where it needs a time range -> the advice leaves on the answer lane under the consult_id it was given, and a fresh turn of the channel voice says it in the channel's own voice

the core cannot answer without knowing more -> the core calls `ask_requester` and its `ask` lane carries the question back (GH #894), the voice puts it in the channel, and the user's reply returns under the SAME consult_id

MODEL DOOR (since 5.1.0, GH #855): `in_model` takes a params-only body -- a model package the colony's llm-registry pushes -- from the composite's own path straight to `./brain`, past the collector, or to `./curator` when `hop.subscriber` ends in `/curator/summarizer`; the receiving llm merges it into its live params and answers nothing.

model.because: the model the brain infers with — a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B
